title: Government Oversight of Care for the Intellectually Disabled
what_it_is: Government Oversight of Care for the Intellectually Disabled

sections.label: MSF and community partners
sections.summary: MSF works with community partners to identify and help persons with intellectual disabilities who have no familial support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: MSF works with community partners such, as the Singapore Police Force (SPF), Social Service Offices (SSOs), Family Service Centres (FSCs), volunteer welfare organisations (VWOs) and disability services providers to identify and help persons with intellectual disabilities with no familial support.

sections.label: Disability support services
sections.summary: Support services include children disability homes, drop-in programmes at Seniors Activity Centres, and Day Activity Centres, with 29 DACs islandwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Some of these support services include the following: (a) children disability homes, which are long-term residential care for children whose caregivers are incapable of caring for them, who have unsafe home environments and/or where their caregivers have passed on; (b) drop-in disability programmes at Seniors Activity Centres, which provide social and recreational programmes for higher functioning persons with disabilities; and (c) Day Activity Centres (DACs), which provide day programmes for persons with disabilities to enhance their independence by equipping them with daily and community living skills.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: There are 29 DACs islandwide, and 19 cater to persons with intellectual disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have added another 400 DAC places in 2017 and will add more this year to increase the availability of such services to persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Vulnerable Adults Bill
sections.summary: The Vulnerable Adults Bill is an additional lever to protect such individuals, to be introduced in Parliament this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: One of the additional levers to protect such individuals is the Vulnerable Adults Bill, which we hope to introduce in Parliament this year.

sections.label: Vulnerable Persons Bill and reporting
sections.summary: The Vulnerable Persons Bill will allow intervention behind closed doors, but requires family, colleagues, neighbours and passers-by to raise suspicions with authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Vulnerable Persons Bill which we intend to introduce will allow us to intervene even behind closed doors, to reach out to families and to reach out behind families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But none of these will be effectual unless family members, colleagues, neighbours and passers-by, people who interact and suspect something amiss is happening to not just persons with intellectual disability but to persons with disabilities, to children and to vulnerable adults, step forward, raise the alarm bell and bring their suspicions to the attention of the authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, I do not have the figures that the Member has asked for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for whether we can expand Public Assistance scheme to help people who are unable to support themselves, we will continue to review our schemes.
